Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the summarization and streaming latency look very promising for our field automation use case. A couple quick clarifying items from our side so we can align internally: 

1) Procurement: we usually buy via PO for any platform > $25k/yr. Is a PO acceptable, or do you require card for the initial term?
2) Marketplace: wondering if Redwood appears in our AWS Marketplace procurement since our finance team prefers to route purchases there for visibility and consolidated billing.
3) Trial success criteria: our engineering team wants to see 10k inference calls/day over a 2-week pilot with <150ms p50 on typical prompts.

I attached the MPA template the legal team will use. Can you confirm whether the POC footprint and the proposed quote align to these criteria and whether billing will start after the trial or immediately?

Best,
Jane
Jane Liu
Head of Data Products
Acme Industrial

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial path & trial conversion readiness — next steps

Hi Jane — great to hear the demo was useful. Quick answers inline then proposed next steps below.

1) Procurement / payment method:
- PO: yes, acceptable. We have a standard PO-based flow for enterprise deals. We typically require a signed Master Subscription Agreement (MSA) + PO before activating long-term billing. For trials we can be flexible: we can run a time-bound pilot without billing until you sign the MSA/PO.
- Card: also supported for faster self-serve trials; lots of customers start on card and convert to PO for renewals.

2) Marketplace: Redwood is listed in the AWS Marketplace (private offers supported). If you prefer marketplace procurement, we can provide an AWS private offer and coordinate with our channel team. There is an extra step for private offers but it preserves consolidated billing.

3) Trial success criteria: 10k calls/day + <150ms p50 is within scope — please note p50 will depend on the exact model variant and sequence length; we’ll set up a baseline run on our staging capacity to validate.

Next steps I propose: 
- Rishi will follow up with a short commercial quote (PO terms vs card options) and attach a time-bound trial plan.
- Dev will scope the staging environment and provide expected p50 numbers for your sample prompts.
- I’ll review the MPA and flag any redlines to legal; if none, we can accept your MPA and issue a PO-friendly quote.

Can we aim to confirm procurement path by end of week? If so, we can start the trial the week after.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Commercial path & trial conversion readiness — next steps

Hi Jane — following Marissa’s note, attaching a short quote with both PO and card options and a proposed POC billing milestone. Key points: 

- Pilot period: 14 calendar days (no charge) — billed only after accepted MSA/PO OR if you explicitly request to move to paid immediately.
- Trial capacity: we’ll provision staging for up to 12k calls/day (buffer above your 10k target) with the standard test model (redwood-small) unless you request a larger variant.
- Billing start: "billing start" will be the date the PO is activated (we can backdate to the end of the pilot if you prefer); otherwise card-start charges begin on the date the trial switches to paid.
- Marketplace private offer: we can prepare a private AWS offer; timeline adds ~3–5 business days for legal/commercial approvals.

Please review the attached and confirm which commercial path you prefer (PO via direct invoice, PO via AWS marketplace private offer, or card). If PO, please share the approver and typical PO lead time so we can plan the go-live.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for the clarity. A few procurement-specific notes: 
- We prefer PO via AWS Marketplace when feasible. If Redwood can provide a private offer with consolidated billing, that’s our preference.
- Typical PO approval lead time once the commercial term sheet is locked is 7–10 business days. We will need your full tax and remit info on the quote.
- For the pilot: procurement is fine with a time-bound trial with billing deferred — as long as the commercial terms that follow are consistent with the quote and private offer.

We’ll aim to have internal sign-off on marketplace approach by Feb 20. Please include a contact in your channel team for the AWS private offer coordination.

-Marcus

Hi Jane / Marcus — quick technical confirmation from the infra side.

We spun up a staging pool that matches the specs we discussed. Observed baseline for your sample prompt set: 
- p50 latency (redwood-small): ~120ms for 256-token average prompt on our staging nodes; p95 ~320ms.
- We can squeeze p50 below 100ms using a quantized variant and dedicated capacity; will require a short capacity reservation (we can include as a line item in the quote).
- We validated continuous throughput to 13k calls/day with steady tail latency inside SLA on the staging job.

If you confirm the AWS private-offer route, channel lead Stephanie (cc’d) will coordinate the marketplace private offer flow. Otherwise if you want to go direct PO, please share approver and billing contact and we’ll prepare invoice-ready paperwork.

Suggested immediate next steps: 
- Marcus: confirm marketplace vs direct PO by Fri Feb 20.
- Jane: confirm pilot start window (we’re targeting week of Feb 23 if procurement aligns).
- Rishi/Marissa: we’ll finalize quote + MPA redlines and hand to legal.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
